t: AI Health and Wellbeing: Triage Ranker — Simple
name: AI Health and Wellbeing: Triage Ranker — Simple
title: AI Health and Wellbeing: Triage Ranker — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] A ranker that orders waiting patients by clinical urgency from vitals and presenting complaint, using a validated scoring rule. It ranks; it never diagnoses. Every rank links to the inputs and the rule version that produced it.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Urgency update: prior 0.2, lik 0.9, marg 0.4 = 0.4500 posterior. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: Architecting Solutions: Building AI for Universal Human Health & Well-being (Chapter)
real_world_basis: Triage scoring rules (e.g., ESI, NEWS) are validated clinical standards; the ranker implements them as software.
signature_version: Signature version: the health Balance assessor — the chapter's A7 Balance (need vs capacity) scored per shift from ranker data, with the 'universal health' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: implement a published validated rule first, calibrate on local data, then rank — never invent a rule.
math_note: Urgency update: prior 0.2, lik 0.9, marg 0.4: 0.4500 posterior [verified]; Rule-validation audit at 95%, p=0.1: 28 samples [verified]
safety: Clinical safety: the ranker is decision support — a clinician confirms every rank before action, and the system fails safe to human triage.
how_it_works: Vitals and complaint feed the scoring rule; the ranker outputs an ordered queue with per-patient score components. The demo recomputes a Bayes urgency update and the audit sample for validating the rule.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
Every numerical claim recomputed at build time

t: AI Health and Wellbeing: Screening Scheduler — Simple
name: AI Health and Wellbeing: Screening Scheduler — Simple
title: AI Health and Wellbeing: Screening Scheduler — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] A scheduler that books preventive screenings by risk and interval: it computes who is due, prioritizes by risk score, and fills slots to minimize missed high-risk patients. Prevention scheduled is prevention delivered.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Benefit retained after 6-month delay (T=24 mo) = 0.8409 fraction. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: Architecting Solutions: Building AI for Universal Human Health & Well-being (Chapter)
real_world_basis: Risk-based screening scheduling is standard in organized screening programs.
signature_version: Signature version: the health Totality assessor — eligible vs screened population as a computed coverage ratio, with the framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: build the eligible registry first, validate risk scores locally, then schedule by risk.
math_note: Benefit retained after 6-month delay (T=24 mo): 0.8409 fraction [verified]; Daily throughput: 96 slots x 0.85 show rate: 81.6 patients [verified]

math_check.label: Daily throughput: 96 slots x 0.85 show rate

safety: Equity safety: the scheduler must not deprioritize by anything but clinical risk — audit for proxy bias quarterly.
how_it_works: Risk registries feed the due-list; the scheduler optimizes slot assignment against no-show models. The demo recomputes the half-life-style decay of screening benefit with delay and the daily throughput.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub

t: AI Health and Wellbeing: Adherence Coach — Simple
name: AI Health and Wellbeing: Adherence Coach — Simple
title: AI Health and Wellbeing: Adherence Coach — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] A coach that helps patients stay on treatment: it learns each patient's barrier pattern (forgetting, side effects, cost, confusion) and times the right nudge — reminder, education, or pharmacist referral. Coaching adapts; nagging doesn't.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Barrier entropy at p=0.4 = 0.9710 bits. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: Architecting Solutions: Building AI for Universal Human Health & Well-being (Chapter)
real_world_basis: Adaptive adherence interventions are evidence-based and deployed in chronic-care programs.
signature_version: Signature version: the health First/Last assessor — treatment start (first) and sustained control (last) anchored per patient journey, with the framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: classify the barrier before choosing the nudge, measure lift per nudge type, and keep a human in the loop for clinical barriers.
math_note: Barrier entropy at p=0.4: 0.9710 bits [verified]; Nudge pipeline: 5 stages x 30 ms: 150 ms [verified]
safety: Autonomy safety: coaching is opt-in, every nudge is skippable, and opting out is one tap — always.
how_it_works: Refill and response data feed a barrier classifier; the coach selects the nudge type per patient and measures lift. The demo recomputes the entropy of the barrier distribution and the latency of the nudge pipeline.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
Every numerical claim recomputed at build time
